To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pre-service secondary teachers have limited perceptions of environmental education, and they have a limited understanding of the constraints to the implementation and practice of environmental education.
The perceptions of secondary pre–service teachers about environmental education and its implementation into practice, are influenced by their experiences and beliefs.

the pre-service teachers in our study: 1) held views about the content, nature and scope of Environmental Education (EE) that were limited; 2) held views that EE should be taught in a particular way; and 3) identified a range of constraints to implementing EE into practice, including: a) lack of time, b) lack of resources, c) lack of teacher training and d) lack of teacher confidence and knowledge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the views of pre-service teachers and how their views may impact on their teaching practice.
how pre-service teachers perceive environmental education and what implications these perceptions may have for pre-service teacher preparation in environmental education.
the views of pre-service teachers and how they might influence their practice as teachers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

pre-service teacher education needs to be more inclusive of environmental education and environmental education needs to be integrated into all aspects of the pre-service teacher education curriculum.

the study revealed that pre-service teachers' perceptions of environmental education and environmental education policy are influenced by their prior learning experiences, their current experiences and their beliefs about the nature and role of environmental education in the curriculum.
the findings of this study have provided a clear understanding of the views of pre-service teachers in relation to environmental education.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

pre-service teachers have a limited perception of the scope of environmental education, and that they perceive constraints to the implementation environmental education into practice, which are likely to limit their practice as environmental educators.

we need to continue to work towards the integration of environmental education into the school curriculum and to provide opportunities for pre-service teachers to develop the knowledge, skills, attitudes and values that will allow them to implement environmental education into practice.
the findings from our study highlight the need to address the perceptions of pre-service teachers about environmental education and its implementation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pre-service teachers are not passive recipients of environmental education, rather they have their own ideas and beliefs that can influence their future practice as teachers.

pre-service teachers should be encouraged to engage with the environmental dimensions of all school subjects, and not just the traditionally associated ones, and that they should be encouraged to develop a critical understanding of the environmental issues that are impacting the lives of young Australians.
pre-service teachers have a strong sense of what is and isn’t environmental education and that they are aware of the constraints they will face as they enter the teaching workforce.
